publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Load data collected in the national load research project in South Africa has shown that residential loads can be modelled as Beta probability distributions, but it has not been evident what Beta parameters should be used. This paper presents a technique for analysing the data to identify the parameters which can best represent the loads and describes how the parameters may be derived from the collected data. Among other things, it is shown that the worst condition for the voltage drop on a radial feeder supplying a finite number of customers depends on both the system demand and the (statistical) variance between the customers, and may not occur at the time of system maximum demand. The selection of Beta parameters for the load model can be associated with the risk that the target voltage drop will be exceeded, linking the load model directly to quality of supply criteria. The techniques can be applied in any country to derive locally appropriate load parameters.

articleTitle: Resonant inversion pulser topology with reduced semiconductor ratings
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: High pulse energy- high pulse repetition rate pulsers are used, among others, to power Pulse-lasers and Pulsed Corona Reactors. To equip these pulsers with reliable all-solid state switching elements has ushered in diverse technologies. To avoid the necessity of using semiconductor stacks or gas-switches on the high voltage side, economic and robust designs favour resonant energy transfer and switching on the low-voltage side with pulse compression on the high-voltage side of a voltage pulse transformer. This paper presents a topology in which maximum use is made of voltage inversion and pulse compression on the low-voltage side to significantly reduce the semiconductor switch burden.

articleTitle: Modelling of steady-state harmonics in a plasma burner plant
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The harmonics produced by three 120 kW AC/DC 6-pulse phase controlled converters introduced resonance into a 380 V system that also supplied the lighting circuits in a Silicon-tetra-fluoride plant. The voltage harmonics produced at this junction resonated with the fluorescent fitting circuits and brought about overheating in the overload trip coils through high-frequency eddy-currents. With two 150 kVA dynamic compensators available from a closed-down plant section, an investigation had to be carried out by modelling to establish the suitability of these compensators for mitigating the harmonics. The paper describes a distortion power theory for analysing the problem. It describes a basic steady-state frequency-domain modelling technique used and then proceeds to validate the model through physical measurement. Lastly, it models the system when the two compensators are installed and makes recommendations for their installation and adjustment.

articleTitle: Benchmark tests and results for the evaluation of L.V. distribution voltage drop calculation procedures
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: There are several approaches to calculating the expected voltage drops in residential low voltage feeders. These methods vary according to their treatment of the uncertainty associated with forecast loads. The calculation algorithms are frequently concealed in sophisticated computer packages where output accuracy is often taken for granted. In this paper issues relating to voltage drop calculation methods are discussed and appropriate benchmark tests are developed and presented with their results. A companion paper investigates the practical verification of probabilistic voltage drop calculation methods using Monte Carlo simulation.

articleTitle: A novel, cost-effective stand-alone generator system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A brushless, doubly-fed stand-alone generator system can have advantages over both conventional as well as converter-based approaches. This paper introduces and discusses the characteristics of a stand-alone generator system based on a brushless, doubly-fed machine (BDFM). Results of steady-state studies are presented for different load and speed conditions. Experimental results using a low power laboratory prototype are presented to illustrate system viability.

articleTitle: Assessment of the monte carlo simulation method for probabilistic feeder voltage drop calculations
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This is a companion paper to one recently published in which benchmark tests were described for the evaluation of LV distribution voltage drop calculation procedures. Monte Carlo simulations are often used when the calculation procedure is based on a probabilistic approach. Many calculation procedures in electrical distribution engineering have been verified using Monte Carlo simulations as a standard. This paper shows that for voltage drop calculations significant inaccuracies may result from this method and that it should be applied with caution

articleTitle: Steady-state and dynamic analyses of isolated self-excited induction generators
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper demonstrates the simplification achieved in the steady-state and dynamic analyses of autonomous self-excited induction generators feeding a general (R-L) load when induction machine equations are expressed in terms of flux linkages. Magnetic saturation of magnetizing path is modelled by expressing the reciprocal of instantaneous magnetizing inductance as a function of saturated air gap (magnetizing) flux linkage. Various steady-state performance results and dynamic responses are shown. Also included is a qualitative study of the induction generator behavior.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Marios Moutzouris is currently a postgraduate student in the Department of Electrical Engineering at the University of the Witwatersrand studying towards the degree of MSc in Software Engineering. He has also completed courses in Software Quality Management. Marios's MSc is entitled “Data Visualization of Low Voltage Networks using a Distributed Virtual Reality Architecture”. Obtained his BSc (Eng.) in Electrical Engineering in 1997.

articleTitle: Aircraft classification using jet engine modulation
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Jet Engine Modulation (JEM) of radar returns is caused by the rotation, relative to the aircraft, of the turbine and its blade assembly. It is the aim of this work to determine the viability of using the modulated returns to recognise aircraft. Data obtained from three aircraft, two jets and a Cessna, was used for the experiments conducted. Classification performance of up to 87% was attained for this limited population.

articleTitle: A study of radio refractivity and super-refractivity in botswana
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A presentation of refractivity variation, based on radiosonde measurements carried out in Maun, northern Botswana, is reported. It is observed that highest afternoon values of surface refractivity occur in February, while the lowest occur in August. It is also noted that for post-midnight periods, the highest value of average surface refractivity occurs in November. A comparison of the average values of surface refractivity, and AN plots, with ITU-R contours, shows reasonable agreement, which can be improved upon with more measurements. Atmospheric ducts, which lead to deep fades and serious interference between radio links, are most prevalent during February afternoons and during the post-midnight periods of November.

articleTitle: Evaluation of converter topologies for power quality solutions
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper several power quality compensator topologies and control algorithms are evaluated on both a simulation and experimental basis. The introduction of various international standards and recommendations on power quality at the point of common coupling the demand to develop cheap, robust multi-functional power quality compensators has emerged from industry. This paper discusses and compares these power quality compensators from an operational and application viewpoint. This is done with the aid of EMTP simulations and experimental results on a 100 kVA multi-functional power quality compensator. The evaluation has been performed on the basis of power quality devices of 2 to 10 MVA power capacity that would be useful on distribution power levels. The main focus of the paper is on power quality compensator topologies with an integrated dip/sag compensation capability.

articleTitle: Visualization of low voltage network designs using a DVR architecture
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In South Africa and other developing countries there is currently a drive to electrify homes of disadvantaged communities. To aid the electrification process requires effective software applications. The set of stand-alone tools currently used are inherently based in two dimensions and convey a limited amount of information. This paper introduces a software application, DataVis, which allows designers to visualize a three-dimensional environment from a two-dimensional CAD drawing. The application allows for the viewing and manipulating of electrical and physical properties of the objects in the environment. A distributed virtual reality software architecture is used to allow networked low-cost personal computers to create and allow the designer to interact with this environment. The concept of using data visualization in three-dimensions will be investigated for its applicability in the electrification design process.

articleTitle: Pm synchronous machine performance calculation based on finite element field solution
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper deals with a performance calculation of a particular design of a permanent magnet synchronous machine. The machine has a solid steel rotor, suitable for high speed operation, excited by buried Samarium-Cobalt permanent magnets. The aim of this paper is to examine two existing methods of performance calculation, based on finite element (FE) magnetic field solutions, in terms of accuracy offered for this specific machine. The three most important quantities chosen for this comparison are stator induced voltage, electromagnetic torque and synchronous reactances. A FE model of the machine is constructed and the magnetic field distribution calculated. Measured results from a prototype machine are compared with predicted results. Conclusions are drawn on the accuracy and applicability of each of the two methods used.

articleTitle: Hybrid techniques using the MoM and PO/UTD: A tutorial overview
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A tutorial review of hybrid computational electromagnetic methods suitable for radio-frequency electromagnetic radiation and scattering problems is presented. The emphasis is on the method of moments (MoM), physical optics (PO) and the uniform theory of diffraction (UTD), and in particular on methods for hydridising them. Such hybrid formulations permit computer simulation of problems sufficiently large electromagnetically to have prohibitive computational requirements using purely the MoM, but not sufficiently large to reliably apply asymptotic methods such as the UTD. Several examples using a commercially available hybrid code are presented, to highlight the advantages of hybrid techniques. A case where the hybrid MOM/PO formulation failed is also reviewed. The industrial use of such codes is discussed, emphasising both the potential power of the approach for complex problems, as well as the advisability of understanding the underlying formulations

articleTitle: Multiple trellis coded Q2PSK: Code design and performance study on fading channels
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper considers the code design, implementation and performance evaluation of Multiple Trellis-Coded Modulation (MTCM) codes for application to Quadrature-Quadrature Phase-Shift Keying (Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>PSK) operating over the mobile fading channel. The benefits in using channel state information based on fading channel estimates in conjunction with the MTCM decoder through a suitable metric weighting function are also considered. The channel estimates are obtained from sequences of known header and pilot symbols embedded in the information stream. This technique is shown to provide remarkably robust performance in the presence of fading. The bit error rate performance of the MTCM code designs (including channel side information), assuming coherent detection and perfect carrier and time synchronization, are then studied by means of simulation for cellular radio channels. It is shown that coding gains in excess of 14.0 dB at a bit error probability of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> can be achieved with the MTCM coded system, relative to the uncoded system on Rayleigh fading channels.

articleTitle: SRMA: Dynamic protocol management for LEO store-and-forward systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: SRMA (Split-Channel Reservation Multiple Access) is examined as a multi-access protocol for store-and-forward systems in narrow band low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication. The protocol mechanism is modelled and the aspects that influence the protocol efficiency are discussed. The optimal operating region for the protocol is determined and a dynamic prediction mechanism is proposed to maintain maximum performance for a mobile user base. Simulations are used to show the effectiveness of this mechanism.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of loss calculations for a planar inductor
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper covers the experimental validation of FEM calculations of losses in a planar inductor under high frequency operating conditions. Thermally controlled experiments are performed at different frequencies in the operating circuit to validate the losses calculated by the FEM.

articleTitle: Neural networks for pneumatic actuator fault detection
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The suitability of artificial neural networks (ANNs) for detecting fault conditions in pneumatic control valve actuators is investigated. Specifically, the ability of a neural network to act as a predictor of correct valve behaviour is examined. Experimental results indicate that standard network architectures are unsuitable for temporal prediction of non-linear system behaviour. An original recurrent network architecture, designed specifically as a predictor and based on autoregressive models and functional approximation is therefore proposed. The performance of this network is evaluated using both measured data and data from simulations based on a mathematical model of the valve. Laboratory implementation of the fault detection system produced encouraging qualitative results, including high success rates for the detection of faults corresponding to valve Coulomb friction changes and input pressure offsets.

articleTitle: 2-Quadrant DC-drive using controllers based on simplified transfer function models
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes a typical experiment performed by 3rd-year electrical engineering students at the University of Stellenbosch. The experiment takes 6 weeks to complete. It is shown that with a high crossover frequency of the drive system open-loop transfer function, and a current-loop that is much faster than the speed-loop, it is possible to use simplified s-domain motor transfer functions to design both the current-loop and speed-loop controllers. The simplifications allow students to concentrate on the task of designing the controllers without being distracted by unnecessary mathematical analysis. Experimental results show that satisfactory drive dynamic behaviour can be achieved despite these simplifications. During the testing of the current-loop performance, students get to appreciate the importance of the current controller as a protective feature.
